rules.title: Owner must give tenant the just cause and rent cap notice in at least 12-point type
rules.requirement: An owner of residential real property subject to Civil Code 1946.2 must give the tenant a notice or lease provision in at least 12-point type. It must state that California law limits rent increases (Civil Code 1947.12) and that after the required period of occupancy a landlord must state a cause in any notice to terminate a tenancy (Civil Code 1946.2). Delivery methods and deadlines for tenancies commenced, renewed or existing before July 1, 2020 (July 1, 2022 for mobilehomes) are in subdivision (f)(1)-(2). The notice is subject to Section 1632.

rules.exemptions: Subdivision (e)(9) excludes housing restricted as affordable by deed, regulatory agreement or recorded document, or subject to an affordable housing subsidy agreement. Subdivision (i) excludes property covered by certain local just cause ordinances. Subdivision (l) excludes homeowners of mobilehomes. The remaining (e) exemptions appear in the neighboring chunk and are not captured here.
rules.interaction: Subdivision (i) says the section does not apply to property subject to a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before 2019-09-01, or to a more protective ordinance adopted or amended after that date, and the property cannot be subject to both. The section is repealed as of 2030-01-01 by its own terms (subdivision (n)). Local ordinance coverage is not encoded and needs review.

rules.title: Owner noncompliance with section voids the written termination notice
rules.requirement: An owner's failure to comply with any provision of Civil Code 1946.2 renders the written termination notice void.
rules.quoted_span:
An owner’s failure to comply with any provision of this section shall render the
written termination notice void.
rules.exemptions: Same exclusions as for the section generally: subdivision (e)(9), the local ordinance carve-outs in (i), and the mobilehome homeowner exclusion in (l). The remaining (e) exemptions are in the neighboring chunk.
rules.interaction: Applies only to property subject to this section. See subdivision (i) on local just cause ordinances. The section is repealed as of 2030-01-01 by its own terms.

rules.title: Owner liable for damages when recovering possession in material violation
rules.requirement: An owner who attempts to recover possession of a rental unit in material violation of the section is liable to the tenant for actual damages and, in the court's discretion, reasonable attorney's fees and costs. On a showing of willful, oppressive, fraudulent or malicious conduct, the award may be up to three times actual damages, and punitive damages may also be awarded. The Attorney General, city attorney or county counsel may seek injunctive relief.
